sections.overview: Idaea emarginata, the Small Scallop, is a geometrid moth recorded widely but not commonly in England and Wales.
sections.habitat: It occupies damp deciduous woodland, meadows and marshes.
sections.diet: The caterpillar is believed to feed on bedstraws (Galium) in the wild; Finnish records also list Galium and Plantago among its food plants.
sections.behavior: Adults fly after dark from June to August and may be attracted to lights, although they can also be flushed by day.
sections.reproduction: The species accounts consulted do not give a reliable clutch size or detailed breeding schedule.
sections.ecology: It belongs to Idaea, the same genus as I. flaveolaria elsewhere in this bestiary; that shared genus alone does not establish a particularly close relationship.
sections.conservation: The British account describes a widespread but uncommon moth; this is a regional description, not a global threat assessment.
